name: What should be included in a bathroom addition quote?

mainEntity.name: What line items should a contractor include so quotes are actually comparable?
mainEntity.text: What line items should a contractor include so quotes are actually comparable?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful bathroom addition quote should be detailed enough to reveal exactly what the contractor is pricing. At minimum, it should list demolition, framing, plumbing rough-in, electrical work, ventilation, waterproofing, tile installation, fixtures, trim, painting, permits, and any allowances for finishes. It should also identify exclusions such as design fees, specialty fixtures, flooring matching, or structural repairs if hidden damage is found. The more specific the quote, the easier it is to compare contractors fairly. Lump-sum proposals can look cheaper at first but may leave out important parts of the project. For a bathroom addition, transparency is especially important because the work usually involves multiple trades and a high chance of unforeseen conditions. A strong quote should make it clear where the cost is fixed and where it could change.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good bathroom addition quote should separate demo, framing, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, waterproofing, tile, fixtures, permits, and allowances. It should also state what is excluded. Vague lump-sum bids make it hard to compare scope and often hide change-order risk.
